tasks.title: ngv2/sink_reachability_gate.py -- NEW deterministic constant-vs-external sink-argument reachability gate
acceptance_criteria: NEW file ngv2/sink_reachability_gate.py exposes assess_sink_reachability(sink_name: str, call_sites: list[str]) -> dict.

Returned dict has EXACTLY these keys: reachable (bool), external_input_sites (list[str]), all_constant (bool), status ('reachable'|'constant_only'), may_confirm (bool); status=='reachable' iff reachable else 'constant_only'; may_confirm==reachable; all_constant==(not reachable).
Edge (a): assess_sink_reachability('os.system', ['os.system("ls")']) -> all_constant=True, reachable=False, may_confirm=False, external_input_sites==[].
Edge (b): assess_sink_reachability('os.system', ['os.system(cmd)']) -> reachable=True, all_constant=False, status='reachable', may_confirm=True, site in external_input_sites.
Edge (d): assess_sink_reachability('os.system', []) -> reachable=False, all_constant=True, status='constant_only', may_confirm=False, external_input_sites==[].

Module is PURE and stdlib-only (ast, typing): no network, clock, randomness, uuid, subprocess, MCP, third-party import, or import of any sibling ngv2/** leaf; no eval/exec/__import__/os.system/subprocess CALL and no decorator (AST enforcer bans them).
Deterministic / differential-fuzzable: identical inputs produce a byte-identical output dict.

spec.objective: Create the NEW pure, stdlib-only single-file module ngv2/sink_reachability_gate.py providing assess_sink_reachability(sink_name, call_sites), the deterministic gate that separates 'the sink fires' from 'attacker input reaches the sink'. Given a sink name and the source snippets of every call site, it AST-classifies each call argument as literal-constant vs externally-influenced and returns whether the sink is attacker-reachable -- so a NobleGreed finding whose dangerous sink is only ever invoked with HARDCODED constant arguments (e.g. the zilliztech/gptcache command-injection) is reported constant_only / may_confirm=False rather than allowed to confirm.
functional_requirements: Expose assess_sink_reachability(sink_name: str, call_sites: list[str]) -> dict returning EXACTLY {reachable: bool, external_input_sites: list[str], all_constant: bool, status: 'reachable'|'constant_only', may_confirm: bool}, with the derived invariants status=='reachable' iff reachable else 'constant_only', may_confirm==reachable, and all_constant==(not reachable).

For each snippet, ast.parse it and walk for ast.Call nodes whose callee bare-name (ast.Name) OR dotted-attribute tail (ast.Attribute.attr) equals sink_name; a dotted sink_name like 'subprocess.run' matches both the dotted form and the bare tail, and only matched calls are inspected.

Classify each positional and keyword argument of a matched call: CONSTANT = ast.Constant (str/num/bytes/bool/None), a tuple/list/dict whose elements are all constant, or a pure constant string concatenation ('a' + 'b' with all operands constant); EXTERNAL = ast.Name, ast.Attribute, ast.Subscript, ast.Call, an ast.JoinedStr (f-string) embedding a FormattedValue/name, or a .format(...)/%-format expression embedding a name.

Aggregate across all sites: if ANY matched call at ANY site has at least one external argument, append that site's source string to external_input_sites in input order de-duplicated and set reachable=True; if every matched call at every site passes only literal constants (or no arguments), set all_constant=True and reachable=False; a snippet that fails to parse, contains no call to sink_name, or whose matched calls take no args contributes no external-input site and does not by itself make the sink reachable; an empty call_sites list yields reachable=False/all_constant=True.

Be PURE, stdlib-only (ast, typing) and deterministic: no network/clock/randomness/uuid/subprocess/MCP/filesystem/logging, no third-party or sibling ngv2/** import, no eval/exec/__import__/os.system/subprocess CALL and no decorator (sink names are processed ONLY as ast data, never executed); identical inputs produce a byte-identical output dict.
spec.interfaces: ngv2/sink_reachability_gate.py exposing assess_sink_reachability(sink_name: str, call_sites: list[str]) -> dict with the fixed 5-key return shape {reachable: bool, external_input_sites: list[str], all_constant: bool, status: 'reachable'|'constant_only', may_confirm: bool}. Pure function; inputs are plain strings; no side effects.
edge_cases: All sites pass only string literals (os.system("ls"), os.system("echo hi")) -> all_constant=True, reachable=False, status='constant_only', may_confirm=False, external_input_sites==[].
One site passes a variable/parameter (os.system(cmd)) -> reachable=True, all_constant=False, status='reachable', may_confirm=True, and that site appears in external_input_sites.
F-string with embedded name (os.system(f"ls {path}")) -> reachable=True, may_confirm=True (embedded path is external).
Empty call_sites [] -> reachable=False, all_constant=True, status='constant_only', may_confirm=False, external_input_sites==[].
Mixed: one constant-only site plus one variable-arg site -> reachable=True and ONLY the variable site in external_input_sites.
Subscript / attribute / nested-call argument (os.system(d["k"]), os.system(obj.attr), os.system(build())) -> external.
Pure constant concatenation os.system("a" + "b") -> constant, NOT reachable.
Dotted sink name matches both subprocess.run(arg)-style dotted calls and the bare tail.
Unparseable snippet contributes no external site and does not make the sink reachable.
Determinism: same inputs -> byte-identical output dict (de-dup preserves input order).
non_goals: Do NOT touch ngv2/verdict.py, ngv2/confidence_signals.py, ngv2/detonation.py, ngv2/session_gate.py, ngv2/gadget_auditor.py, or any other existing module.

Do NOT implement the downstream INTEGRATION wiring (making the live verdict path call assess_sink_reachability and demote/refuse a constant_only confirmed verdict) -- that is a SEPARATE downstream edit leaf and is out of scope; this is a pure-module leaf so no integration test is required.
Do NOT add real dataflow/SSA/taint/symbolic execution, inter-procedural call resolution, network, filesystem reads, wall-clock, randomness, subprocess, or logging.
Do NOT import any third-party package or any sibling ngv2/** leaf.
Do NOT introduce any eval/exec/__import__/os.system/subprocess CALL or any decorator; sink names are processed ONLY as ast data, never executed.
Do NOT author or modify any test -- the committed oracle tests/ngv2/test_sink_reachability_gate_wired.py is authoritative.
spec.implementation_notes:
WHOLE-FILE single-file emission of a NEW file (never a __JANUSMASK_PATCHES__ symbol patch, never a manifest, never a dotted qualname). Use only `import ast` and `typing`. Define a helper that returns the sink tail name for matching: for ast.Call, callee may be ast.Name (compare .id) or ast.Attribute (compare .attr to the tail of sink_name); if sink_name is dotted, the comparison tail is sink_name.split('.')[-1] and a bare callee name equal to that tail also matches. Define _is_constant(node) recursively: True for ast.Constant; for ast.Tuple/ast.List all elts constant; for ast.Dict all keys+values constant; for ast.BinOp with op ast.Add where both operands are constant (covers 'a' + 'b'); otherwise False. Treat as EXTERNAL: ast.Name, ast.Attribute, ast.Subscript, ast.Call, ast.JoinedStr containing any ast.FormattedValue, and a .format(...) call or %-BinOp whose operands embed a Name/Attribute/Subscript/Call. Iterate call_sites in order; wrap ast.parse in try/except (SyntaxError/ValueError) and skip unparseable snippets. For each matched ast.Call, inspect node.args and [kw.value for kw in node.keywords]; if any arg is not _is_constant, mark the site external (append site string once, preserving input order). After all sites: reachable = bool(external_input_sites); all_constant = not reachable; status = 'reachable' if reachable else 'constant_only'; may_confirm = reachable. Return a freshly built dict with the keys in fixed order to guarantee byte-stable output.

# CREDENTIAL-NAMING CONSTRAINT (the AST security gate FAILS the build if a variable whose name contains (case-insensitive) "password", "secret", or "key" is assigned a string literal -- it reads as a hardcoded credential even though this is an external clean-room target with no real secret). NEVER bind a string literal to such a variable. Use a neutral name instead (field_name, check_id, label, name, ident, column) or iterate a collection literal / build the mapping from a list of tuples. This applies to dict keys held in a temp var, field labels, and constant identifiers.

# STDLIB-ONLY CONSTRAINT (the verification environment installs NO third-party packages, so importing one fails collection -> the whole build is rolled back and the leaf is parked). Import ONLY the Python standard library. Import NO third-party package: NO pydantic, NO pydantic_settings, NO attrs, NO pyyaml, NO numpy, NO requests, etc. For data models / config use stdlib dataclasses (dataclasses.dataclass), enum.Enum, typing, and plain dict / json instead of pydantic BaseModel / BaseSettings. If the spec mentions pydantic-style validation, re-express it with stdlib dataclasses + manual checks.

# DETERMINISM CONSTRAINT (the AST nondeterminism gate FAILS the build if it sees a wall-clock or nondeterministic source). Do NOT call datetime.now / datetime.utcnow, time.time / time.monotonic, unseeded random, uuid, os.urandom, or secrets to obtain a timestamp / id / randomness. Instead accept any timestamp, seed, or clock as an EXPLICIT parameter with a deterministic default (the oracle injects it, e.g. via now_fn / make_scripted_clock), so the same inputs always produce the same output.


# COMMITTED ORACLE CONTRACT (authoritative; you cannot read these files at synthesis time so they are reproduced verbatim -- your code MUST make them pass):

## tests/ngv2/test_sink_reachability_gate_wired.py
```python
"""RED oracle for ngv2.sink_reachability_gate -- the deterministic constant-vs-
external sink-argument reachability gate. Separates "the sink fires" from
"attacker input reaches the sink": if a dangerous sink is only ever called with
HARDCODED constant arguments, no attacker input can reach it and the finding MUST
NOT be allowed to confirm.

A PURE, stdlib-only (ast) tool: assess_sink_reachability(sink_name, call_sites)
-> {reachable, external_input_sites, all_constant, status, may_confirm}. For each
snippet it AST-parses and finds Call nodes whose bare-name or dotted tail equals
sink_name, then classifies each argument as constant (Constant / const
tuple/list/dict / pure const concat) or external (Name/Attribute/Subscript/Call/
f-string-with-name/.format/%-format with a name). Byte-stable determinism.

This oracle is the *_wired reachability proof: importing assess_sink_reachability
from the live ngv2.sink_reachability_gate module is the wiring contract.
"""
import json

from ngv2.sink_reachability_gate import assess_sink_reachability

RESULT_KEYS = {'reachable', 'external_input_sites', 'all_constant', 'status',
               'may_confirm'}


# --- contract: fixed-shape dict + invariants -------------------------------
def test_return_shape_contract():
    res = assess_sink_reachability('os.system', ['os.system("ls")'])
    assert set(res) == RESULT_KEYS
    assert isinstance(res['reachable'], bool)
    assert isinstance(res['external_input_sites'], list)
    assert isinstance(res['all_constant'], bool)
    assert res['status'] in ('reachable', 'constant_only')
    assert isinstance(res['may_confirm'], bool)


def test_status_allconstant_mayconfirm_invariants():
    for sites in (['os.system("ls")'], ['os.system(cmd)'], []):
        res = assess_sink_reachability('os.system', sites)
        assert res['status'] == ('reachable' if res['reachable'] else 'constant_only')
        assert res['may_confirm'] == res['reachable']
        assert res['all_constant'] == (not res['reachable'])


# --- (a) all sites pass only string literals -> constant_only --------------
def test_all_constant_string_args_is_constant_only():
    res = assess_sink_reachability('os.system', ['os.system("ls")', 'os.system("echo hi")'])
    assert res['all_constant'] is True
    assert res['reachable'] is False
    assert res['status'] == 'constant_only'
    assert res['may_confirm'] is False
    assert res['external_input_sites'] == []


# --- (b) a site passes a variable -> reachable -----------------------------
def test_variable_arg_is_reachable():
    res = assess_sink_reachability('os.system', ['os.system(cmd)'])
    assert res['reachable'] is True
    assert res['all_constant'] is False
    assert res['status'] == 'reachable'
    assert res['may_confirm'] is True
    assert 'os.system(cmd)' in res['external_input_sites']


# --- (c) f-string with embedded name -> reachable --------------------------
def test_fstring_with_name_is_reachable():
    res = assess_sink_reachability('os.system', ['os.system(f"ls {path}")'])
    assert res['reachable'] is True
    assert res['may_confirm'] is True


# --- (d) empty call_sites -> constant_only ---------------------------------
def test_empty_call_sites_is_constant_only():
    res = assess_sink_reachability('os.system', [])
    assert res['reachable'] is False
    assert res['all_constant'] is True
    assert res['status'] == 'constant_only'
    assert res['may_confirm'] is False
    assert res['external_input_sites'] == []


# --- mixed: only the variable site is recorded -----------------------------
def test_mixed_sites_records_only_external_site():
    sites = ['os.system("ls")', 'os.system(user_cmd)']
    res = assess_sink_reachability('os.system', sites)
    assert res['reachable'] is True
    assert res['external_input_sites'] == ['os.system(user_cmd)']


# --- subscript / attribute / nested-call args are external -----------------
def test_subscript_attribute_and_call_args_are_external():
    for site in ('os.system(d["k"])', 'os.system(obj.attr)', 'os.system(build())'):
        res = assess_sink_reachability('os.system', [site])
        assert res['reachable'] is True, site


# --- pure constant concatenation is constant -------------------------------
def test_constant_string_concat_is_constant():
    res = assess_sink_reachability('os.system', ['os.system("a" + "b")'])
    assert res['reachable'] is False
    assert res['all_constant'] is True


# --- dotted sink name matches dotted call and bare tail --------------------
def test_dotted_sink_name_matches_dotted_and_tail():
    res = assess_sink_reachability('subprocess.run', ['subprocess.run(arg)'])
    assert res['reachable'] is True
    res2 = assess_sink_reachability('subprocess.run', ['run(arg)'])
    assert res2['reachable'] is True


# --- unparseable snippet contributes no external site ----------------------
def test_unparseable_snippet_contributes_nothing():
    res = assess_sink_reachability('os.system', ['os.system($$$ not python'])
    assert res['reachable'] is False
    assert res['external_input_sites'] == []


# --- determinism -----------------------------------------------------------
def test_output_is_byte_stable_deterministic():
    sites = ['os.system("ls")', 'os.system(cmd)', 'os.system(f"x {y}")']
    a = json.dumps(assess_sink_reachability('os.system', sites), sort_keys=True)
    b = json.dumps(assess_sink_reachability('os.system', sites), sort_keys=True)
    assert a == b

```
